settings.about.summary: Local-first security center. One Go binary that runs on your machine and reports dependency vulnerabilities, licence issues, IaC misconfigurations and leaked secrets for GitHub repositories, local directories and Docker images in one view. Built on Trivy, Gitleaks and OSV; nothing leaves the machine except the documented network calls.
settings.about.author: Built by
settings.about.support: Bastion is free and open source. If it helps you, you can support its development.
settings.epss.title: EPSS exploit scores
settings.epss.body: At most once a day, downloads the FIRST.org EPSS feed — a ~2.8 MB gzipped CSV from epss.empiricalsecurity.com — to rank findings by how likely each CVE is to be exploited. Nothing is uploaded.
settings.reach.title: Go reachability
settings.reach.body: Runs govulncheck on Go repositories to tell whether vulnerable code is actually called, not just present. Uses vuln.go.dev for advisories and proxy.golang.org (or your GOPROXY) for module downloads; nothing about the scan is uploaded.
settings.reach.install: Install Go; findings stay unknown until then.
settings.outdated.title: Outdated packages
settings.outdated.body: Looks up the latest version of each package on deps.dev (api.deps.dev) during scans. Only ecosystems, package names and versions are sent.
settings.eol.title: End-of-life check
settings.eol.body: Checks the scanned operating system and Go version against endoflife.date during scans. Only the product name is sent; versions are compared locally.
settings.rules.title: Noise rules
settings.rules.body: Close matching findings now and in later scans. Malware is never closed by a rule, and a secret only by a rule of the Secret type.
settings.rules.proposed: Proposed by an agent, closes nothing until approved
settings.sast.title: SAST
settings.sast.body: Downloads Opengrep {version} (~47 MB) and the community rules (~1.1 MB) from GitHub, then scans repository source locally for code issues. Both downloads are checksum-verified.
settings.sast.notInstalled: Not installed yet; the next scan downloads it.
settings.notifications.title: Notifications
settings.notifications.body: After a scan adds new findings at or above the chosen severity, posts a short summary to Slack. The first scan of a project sends nothing.
settings.notifications.emailHint: Requires STARTTLS (submission port 587); there is no plain-text fallback.
settings.ai.title: Local AI
settings.ai.body: Explains a finding with a model on your machine. Off by default; nothing is sent anywhere except the loopback endpoint you configure, and the answer is advisory.
settings.ai.endpointHint: An OpenAI-compatible URL on a loopback address or localhost, for example Ollama's default.
settings.ai.modelHint: The model name the server expects. A local model must be pulled before it can answer.
settings.ai.modelsFailedUnknown: Could not list models; see the server log.
settings.ai.saveFailed: Could not save the AI settings.
settings.ai.modelRequired: Choose a model before turning this on.
settings.licence.title: Licence policy
settings.licence.description: The policy for every project. An allowed licence is hidden; a denied one stays visible at high severity. Matching is exact, so “MIT OR Apache-2.0” is its own entry.
settings.release.title: Release check
settings.release.body: At most once a day, asks github.com for the newest bastion release tag. Sends your IP and User-Agent; nothing else leaves your machine.
settings.release.available: {version} is available; the sidebar shows the upgrade command.
settings.mcp.title: MCP server
settings.mcp.body: bastion mcp connects your AI agent to Bastion, so it can work with your scan data directly. Scanner text is returned as untrusted data.
